name: Tundra Wolf
body:
TUNDRA WOLF
CR 2

A hulking wolf with grayish-white fur stalks toward you as howls echo in the distance.

XP 600
N Medium animal
Init +4; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 12, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +4 natural)
hp 25 (3d8+12)
Fort +9, Ref +7, Will +3

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee bite +5 (1d6+4 plus trip)
Special Attacks howl, pack attack

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 15, Con 18, Int 2, Wis 14, Cha 10
Base Atk +2; CMB +5; CMD 17 (21 vs. trip)
Feats Endurance B, Great Fortitude, Run
Skills Perception +6, Stealth +6, Survival +6 (+10 tracking by scent); Racial Modifiers +4 Survival when tracking by scent
SQ tireless

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Howl (Ex)

As a standard action, a lone tundra wolf’s howl causes animals within 30 feet to become frightened for 1 round and shaken for 1d6 rounds thereafter (DC 11 Will negates). If multiple tundra wolves howl simultaneously, the save DC increases by 1 for each additional wolf, to a maximum of DC 16, and the radius of the howl increases by 5 feet for each additional wolf. Predatory animals have a +4 bonus on their save, and animals with at least 8 Hit Dice are immune.

Pack Attack (Ex)

Tundra wolves surge in close to attack their foes. Two tundra wolves can share the same square and are considered to be flanking if both attack the same target. A tundra wolf’s movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity when leaving a square it shares with another tundra wolf.

Tireless (Ex)

A tundra wolf has a +4 bonus on saving throws or Constitution checks against becoming fatigued or exhausted.

Tundra wolves have pale fur, often with a shaggy ruff and wide paws and long legs to run down prey and drive them to exhaustion as they pursue them relentlessly over vast distances. They are larger than typical wolves, often well over 100 pounds.

The howls of tundra wolves are terrifying to prey, but they also bind pack members together, calling fellows to the hunt, communicating the location of one another (and potential food sources), and even determining social hierarchy within the pack. Howls can be heard echoing over vast distances and help packs define their range, which may extend more than 50 miles across.
